**Sikhae (식해)** – a Korean “raw‑fish” dish that’s simple, fresh, and full of flavor. It’s usually served cold, with a tangy, slightly spicy dipping sauce, and is perfect for a light lunch or a refreshing starter. --- ## 1. What You’ll Need | Category | Item | Notes | |----------|------|-------| | **Fish & Seafood** | • Fresh white fish (e.g., sea bream, yellow croaker, snapper)
• Shrimp (peeled, deveined)
• Squid (cleaned, sliced)
• Mussels or clams (optional) | Buy the freshest you can find; the better the fish, the tastier the dish. | | **Vegetables & Garnish** | • Green onions (thinly sliced)
• Sesame seeds (toasted)
• Chili flakes or fresh red pepper (optional) | Adds crunch and a pop of color. | | **Sauce Ingredients** | • Soy sauce (2 tbsp)
• Rice vinegar (1 tbsp)
• Sesame oil (1 tsp)
• Garlic (minced, 1 tsp)
• Sugar or honey (½ tsp)
• Salt & pepper (to taste) | Adjust sweetness and saltiness to your preference. | | **Tools** | • Sharp knife
• Cutting board
• Small bowl (for sauce)
• Serving platter or shallow bowl | A clean, sharp knife is essential for thin, even slices. | --- ## 2. Step‑by‑Step Instructions ### Step 1: Prepare the Fish & Seafood 1. **Clean & Trim** - Rinse the fish under cold water. - Remove scales, guts, and any dark flesh. - Pat dry with paper towels. 2. **Slice Thinly** - Place the fish on a chilled cutting board. - Slice into ¼‑inch thick pieces, cutting against the grain for tenderness. - If you’re using shrimp or squid, slice them into bite‑size pieces. 3. **Optional – Quick Blanch** - For mussels/clams, briefly blanch in boiling water for 30 s, then rinse in ice water to stop cooking. - This keeps them firm and removes excess slime. ### Step 2: Make the Dipping Sauce 1. In a small bowl, whisk together: - 2 Tbsp soy sauce - 1 Tbsp rice vinegar - 1 tsp sesame oil - 1 tsp minced garlic - ½ tsp sugar (or honey) - Pinch of salt & pepper 2. Taste and adjust: - More vinegar for acidity, more soy for saltiness, or a pinch of chili flakes for heat. ### Step 3: Assemble the Dish 1. **Arrange the Fish** - On a chilled platter or shallow bowl, lay the fish slices in a single layer. - If you have multiple types of fish, arrange them in separate sections for variety. 2. **Add Seafood** - Sprinkle shrimp, squid, and/or mussels over the fish. 3. **Garnish** - Scatter thinly sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds over everything. - Add a few chili flakes if you like a bit of spice. 4. **Serve Immediately** - Place the sauce in a small bowl on the side. - Encourage diners to dip each piece into the sauce before eating. --- ## 3. Tips & Variations | Tip | Why It Helps | |-----|--------------| | **Keep Everything Cold** | Raw fish tastes best when chilled. Keep the platter in the fridge until just before serving. | | **Use a Sharp Knife** | Thin, even slices reduce the risk of biting into tough muscle fibers. | | **Freshness Is Key** | The dish relies on the natural flavor of the fish; avoid pre‑marinated or canned options. | | **Add a Splash of Citrus** | A squeeze of lemon or lime over the fish before serving brightens the flavors. | | **Try Different Fish** | Sea bream, yellow croaker, snapper, or even tuna work well. Mix and match for a colorful plate. | | **Make a “Sikhae‑Guk” Soup** | Some families serve a light broth (made from fish stock, kelp, and a touch of soy sauce) alongside the raw fish. It’s optional but adds depth. | --- ## 4. Serving Suggestions - **With Rice** – Serve a small bowl of steamed white rice on the side for a balanced meal. - **With Kimchi** – A small portion of mild kimchi pairs nicely, adding a fermented kick. - **With a Light Salad** – Toss mixed greens with a light vinaigrette to complement the raw fish. --- ### Quick Recap 1. **Clean & slice** fresh fish and seafood. 2. **Whisk** a simple soy‑vinegar‑sesame sauce. 3. **Arrange** fish, add seafood, garnish, and serve cold. Enjoy the clean, briny taste of *sikhae*—a true celebration of fresh seafood!
